findings.breaking_input: An adapter containing a string with the pattern `from '<name>'` in its text, e.g. `export async function verify(ctx){const n="see from 'api-reference' for the format";const r=await ctx.fetch("https://api.example.com/v");return{ok:r.ok,answerer:"api.example.com"};}` — the `zero-dep-leg` lint reports `imports package api-reference` and refuses the adapter.
findings.why: stripComments blanks comments but intentionally keeps string literals so that real specifiers (which live in quotes) survive. The specifier regex /\bfrom\s*["']([^"']+)["']/g is then run on that comment-stripped, string-preserving text, so `from 'api-reference'` inside an arbitrary string matches as if it were an import statement. The twin of the fixed verifyBody defect (token inside a string treated as code) survives in specifiers: the fix applied the one-pass tokenizer to verifyBody but left specifiers scanning raw string content. The AMBIENT check two lines below correctly re-blanks strings, but the specifier pass does not.
findings.fix: After stripComments, also blank string contents for the specifier scan (same replace as the AMBIENT pass), or restrict the from/import regex to only match when the quoted specifier is preceded by an actual import/export keyword in unquoted code context. Add a scan-probe case `stringFrom: 'const s = "from \\"pkg\\"";'` asserting clean.

findings.breaking_input: A checkout with CRLF line endings (Windows git autocrlf=true): `sed 's/^      - api\.cloudflare\.com$/      - com/'` produces no replacement because the line is `      - api.cloudflare.com\r` and the `$` anchor in sed sits after the `\r`, so `com$` does not match. The `! cmp -s` guard then fires and the test fails with 'fixture edit did not land'.
findings.why: Twin of the CRLF-literal-edit defect fixed in launch-lint.mjs's baseline(). The baseline() fix normalises to LF before applying indexOf/replace edits, but the bats test edits the checked-out registry file via sed with a `$` end-of-line anchor. On a CRLF file the `\r` sits between the last character and the `$` anchor, so the pattern silently fails to match. The CI legs are Linux (LF) so CI stays green; a local Windows developer running the suite hits a red test that looks like a lint regression.
findings.fix: Either strip `\r` before the sed (`tr -d '\r' < file | sed ...`), or use a pattern without the `$` anchor (`s/      - api\.cloudflare\.com/      - com/`), matching the same normalise-then-edit approach the lint self-test already uses.
